title: Gendered motives for group formidability among children and adults
title_zh: 儿童与成年人群体威慑性别动机
abstract: Recent decades have seen a surge of research revealing the core, early emerging psychological building blocks for navigating human societies. Yet, how such core motives operate across life, undergirding political ideology, remains unknown. Here we use the same kind of minimal, abstract group stimuli across the lifespan to show that gendered preferences for majority groups manifest among preschoolers and adults alike (but not among preverbal infants) and that they motivate support for sustaining intergroup hierarchies (for example, ethnic persecution, militarism and social welfare opposition) among adults. Preschool (N = 317) boys, but not girls, preferred majority rather than minority members, whereas infants (N = 180) chose randomly between the two. Among adults (N = 3,467), males also liked the majority more than females, and these coalitional preferences correlated robustly with political ideology. These results indicate that gendered motives for intergroup formidability are rooted in earliest childhood once children begin navigating peer relationships independently. Fonn et al. find that boys but not girls prefer larger groups by age three, and these preferences predict support for group-based hierarchy among adults. This suggests that gendered motives for intergroup formidability are rooted in earliest childhood.
abstract_zh: 近年来，大量研究揭示了人类社会导航的核心、早期出现的心理基石。然而，这些核心动机在一生中如何运作，以及它们如何支撑政治立场，目前仍未知。本研究使用跨生命周期的相同简抽象群体刺激，展示了性别化的多数群体偏好在学龄前儿童和成年人中均有体现（但非在婴儿期），且这些偏好激励成年人维持群体间等级制度（例如种族迫害、军国主义和反社会福利）。在学龄前（N = 317）中，男孩而非女孩更倾向于选择多数成员；而在婴儿（N = 180）中，选择在两者之间随机进行。在成年人（N = 3,467）中，男性比女性更倾向于多数群体，且这些联盟偏好与政治立场呈 robust 相关。这些结果表明，一旦儿童开始独立处理同伴关系，性别化的群体威慑动机就根植于最早的童年。Fonn 等人发现，男孩但不是女孩在三岁时更倾向于较大的群体，且这些偏好预测成年人对基于群体的等级制度的支持。这表明，性别化的群体威慑动机根植于最早的童年。
